moderate_claims.claim_text: ASPI/QLE has definitive agreements with TerraPower: a $22M (10% OID) term loan to partially fund construction of a uranium enrichment facility in Pelindaba, South Africa, plus an Initial Supply Agreement and a 10-year Long-Term Supply Agreement of up to 150 metric tons of HALEU (2028-2037).
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('ASP Isotopes') -> 340 hits, top hits ASPI self-filings
edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Quantum Leap Energy') -> 105 hits, top hits ASPI self-filings

edgar_fts.query_fulltext('TerraPower') -> 155 hits across SEC filings — top hits are Uranium Energy Corp 8-K (2023), Centrus 8-K (2020), and ASPI 10-Q (2025-08-14). TerraPower itself is private (Bill Gates / Cascade Investment)
TerraPower is privately-held — no counterparty 10-K filings exist for direct corroboration (Heuristic 7 limited)
moderate_claims.M_check: Counterparty disclosure on the TerraPower side is structurally unavailable (private company). The supply window starts 2028 — Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational, extra weight): 150 MT HALEU is large enough to be the entire HALEU output of multiple commercial enrichers for years (US HALEU production is currently <1 MT/year). Promise of 150 MT over 2028-2037 vs ASPI/QLE's status (no operating commercial enrichment facility, no DOE HALEU contract, no NRC enrichment license — see C2) is the classic Heuristic 3 stage gap.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Term loan ($22M with 10% OID = $19.8M cash) is verifiable in principle from ASPI cash flow disclosure (not part of M-source check here). The HALEU supply agreement is a binding contract per the filing, but is conditioned on facility construction completing and on commercial enrichment capability that ASPI does not yet have. Counterparty silence is structural, not adverse. Heuristic 3 stage gap is the binding concern: 150 MT HALEU by 2037 from a pre-construction facility is aggressive. MODE — not RED, because the binding term loan provides some discipline that the deal is real, but the production-volume claim is far ahead of operating stage.

moderate_claims.claim_text: In January 2026 ASPI acquired Renergen (formerly JSE:REN / ASX:RLT), South Africa's leading onshore natural gas explorer and first integrated producer of liquid helium and LNG; Renergen has IDC and DFC indebtedness and the DFC has conditionally approved up to $500M senior secured debt for Phase 2 of the Virginia Gas Project (~$1B+ build).
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Renergen') -> 75 hits across SEC filings — top hits are ASPI 8-Ks announcing the deal
Renergen was a JSE / ASX dual-listed entity prior to acquisition — foreign-listing record not in catalog (Heuristic 2)
DFC (US International Development Finance Corporation) loans are not flowed through USAspending in the standard contract/grant pipeline — coverage gap (Heuristic 5)
moderate_claims.M_check: Renergen's pre-acquisition existence as a JSE/ASX filer is verifiable in principle from those exchanges (not in catalog). The $500M DFC debt is 'conditionally approved' — a stage characterization that is one step short of 'committed' or 'drawn'. DFC conditional approvals are commitments contingent on satisfaction of conditions precedent that frequently take 12-24+ months to satisfy, and the Virginia Gas Project Phase 2 build cost (~$1B+) means the DFC tranche covers <50% — equity / mezz gap of $500M+ needs to be raised on top.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Acquisition is internally consistent across ASPI filings and verifiable via foreign-exchange delisting records. The pivot concern is the Heuristic 3 stage gap on the DFC funding: 'conditionally approved up to $500M' is being narrated alongside Phase 2 of a $1B+ build — without disclosure of the conditions precedent or the unfunded equity gap. MODE — not on the acquisition itself, but on the implied DFC-funded build pathway. Watch list: next 10-K disclosure of DFC conditions satisfaction is the natural follow-up.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Jan 2026 Prepayment Agreement with Meta Platforms to develop a 1.2 GW power campus in Pike County, OH.
moderate_claims.M_check: Meta SEC filings search for 'Oklo' yields 0 hits since 2025-01-01 (Heuristic 7 — counterparty-disclosure threshold).
moderate_claims.interpretation: The Prepayment Agreement is dated Jan 5, 2026. Meta has filed multiple 10-K/10-Q since then but does not yet mention Oklo by name. Under Heuristic 7, a real prepayment from a hyperscaler for 1.2 GW of nuclear power would likely be material to Meta. However, the deal is recent and the prepayment mechanism may not yet have triggered any disclosed cash flow on Meta's side, so MODE rather than RED. Watch list — counterparty corroboration absent. Also note: this is a 'prepayment / mechanism to advance powerhouse deployment', NOT a binding long-term PPA at fixed price. Classic Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational) stage gap — no powerhouse yet built or NRC-licensed.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Dec 2024 12 GW Master Power Agreement with Switch, Ltd., 'one of the largest corporate PPAs in history'.
supports: Switch is privately held (acquired by IFM/DigitalBridge 2022) - no SEC filings to corroborate, so Heuristic 7 limited
Heuristic 3 - 'Master Power Agreement' framework deal, not firm PPA with delivery schedule
moderate_claims.M_check: Counterparty-disclosure check unavailable (private). Apply Heuristic 3 with extra weight: 12 GW vs Oklo's installed base = 0 MW and no NRC license. 12 GW equals ~160 Aurora powerhouses; even Oklo's first-of-kind powerhouse is not yet built.
moderate_claims.interpretation: 'Master Power Agreement' is a framework — not a binding PPA with specific MW/date/price commitments per the Heuristic 3 stage ladder. Magnitude (12 GW = ~160 reactors) is implausibly large versus Oklo's actual stage (no licensed unit; first INL Aurora not yet built). Marketing language ('one of the largest corporate PPAs in history') is hyperbolic relative to legal substance. Counterparty corroboration unavailable because Switch is private — UNVERIFIABLE on M-side, but framework discipline (planned vs operational) flags as MODE.

moderate_claims.claim_text: HALEU Energy Fuel Inc. (NNE subsidiary) has a Memorandum of Understanding dated March 30, 2023 with Centrus Energy Corp for HALEU fuel supply collaboration.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('HALEU Energy Fuel') -> 27 hits, ALL NNE self-filings
moderate_claims.M_check: Centrus (LEU CIK 0001065059) is a public US filer (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K). A March 2023 MoU with NNE is now 3+ years old. Centrus filings make ZERO references to either 'Nano Nuclear' or 'HALEU Energy Fuel'. Per Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold), a real ongoing HALEU supply arrangement with a Tier-1 enricher would typically appear at least in customer/partner narrative — but Heuristic 4 also applies: an MoU is non-binding, below the materiality threshold for Centrus 10-K disclosure of a small counterparty.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Counterparty silence on a 3-year-old MoU with a small pre-revenue counterparty is consistent with Heuristic 4 (non-binding strategic understanding, not material to the larger party). However, the asymmetry — NNE keeps citing 'HALEU Energy Fuel' in 27 filings, Centrus in 0 — suggests the MoU has not progressed to operating substance. Stage gap (planned/intent vs operating supply contract): MODE. Not RED, because the claim itself is staged as an 'MOU', not as a binding supply contract.
